articles.title: Jerry Koosman Dies at 83, World Series Champion Won 222 Games as Pitcher Across 19 MLB Seasons
articles.summary: Former MLB starting pitcher Jerry Koosman, who spent the majority of his career with the New York Mets, has died at the age of 83.
articles.body:
Former MLB starting pitcher Jerry Koosman, who spent the majority of his career with the New York Mets, has died at the age of 83.

"We are saddened to share the news that Jerry Koosman has passed away," the Mets announced Sunday. "We send our thoughts and prayers to his family."

Koosman played for the Mets, Minnesota Twins, Chicago White Sox and Philadelphia Phillies across his 19-year MLB career from 1967-85.

He earned two All-Star nods and won a World Series title with New York in 1969.

Koosman compiled a record of 222-209 across 612 total appearances throughout his career, including 527 starts. 140 of his wins came as a member of the Mets, ranking No. 3 on their all-time leaderboard .

Koosman spent his first 12 seasons in New York, quickly developing into a key piece of the team's rotation.

In the 1969 World Series, the Mets won both of his starts against the Baltimore Orioles. This included a complete game in Game 5 of the series, as New York secured a 5-3 win to capture the franchise's first championship.

The left-hander owned a 3.09 ERA during his Mets tenure before he was eventually traded to the Twins in exchange for relief pitcher Jesse Orosco in 1978.

Koosman spent just over two seasons in Minnesota, finishing with a 39-35 record across 83 starts. He was later dealt to the White Sox in the middle of his 1981 campaign.

Koosman would go on to play for Chicago over the next two years before spending his final pair of MLB seasons in Philadelphia, finally retiring from pitching at the age of 42 years old.

Through his 19 years in the majors, he tallied 2,556 strikeouts compared to 1,198 walks while recording 140 complete games. He also boasted a 3.36 ERA.

Koosman was inducted into the New York Mets Hall of Fame in 1989 before his No. 36 was retired by the club in Aug. 2021.

articles.title: MLB Gold Glove Awards 2026 Full List of Winners and Reaction
articles.summary: The best defensive players in MLB were honored on Sunday.
articles.body:
The best defensive players in MLB were honored on Sunday.

With the season officially coming to a close last week, the 2026 Gold Glove Awards were handed out. Here's a look at this year's winners.

SS: Geraldo Perdomo, Arizona Diamondbacks

RF: Corbin Carroll, Arizona Diamondbacks

Gabriel Moreno winning a Gold Glove makes him the second catcher ever to win a Gold Glove and a batting title in the same season. He joins Minnesota Twins legend Joe Mauer, who achieved the feat in 2008 and 2009.

Moreno slashed .311/.388/.486 with 16 home runs and 83 RBI this year.

With teammates Corbin Carroll and Geraldo Perdomo joining him as Gold Glove winners, the trio became the third group of Diamondbacks players to win the award in the same year.

Dillon Dingler took home his second consecutive Gold Glove, making him the fourth Detroit Tigers player to win the award multiple times and the first since Iván Rodríguez in 2007.

Alex Bregman, who won his second Gold Glove Award, is just the second Cubs third baseman to have won the award, joining Hall of Famer Ron Santo. His teammate, Pete Crow-Armstrong, won his second consecutive Gold Glove.

Mauricio Dubón is in a league of his own when it comes to utility players winning Gold Gloves. He's already won it three times since it was first awarded to utility players in 2022.

For Brice Turang and Jackson Chourio, taking home Gold Glove Awards makes their season even sweeter. Those two helped lead the Brewers to their first World Series title in franchise history, beating the Tampa Bay Rays in five games.

articles.title: 2026 Gold Glove: Pete Crow-Armstrong, Jackson Chourio, Alex Bregman take the honor alongside several first-time winners
articles.summary: Nine of the 20 total 2026 Gold Glove recipients earned the award for the first time.
articles.body:
With the 2026 MLB season coming to an end, the award season is underway. On Sunday, MLB announced the 20 recipients of the Gold Glove awards, with a number of big names and new faces taking home the hardware.

The Gold Glove, which honors the best defensive players in the league, is handed out to one player for each position in the two leagues. This year's honorees included nine first-time winners, nearly half of the total field.

Pete Crow-Armstrong got his offseason started with his second Gold Glove in two seasons. The Chicago Cubs center fielder, who took home his first Gold Glove honor last year, won again after putting up one of the best defensive seasons in baseball.

Crow-Armstrong's dominant batting and 40-40 season have made him a strong NL MVP candidate, but he took home another piece of hardware first.

Crow-Armstrong's Cubs teammate Alex Bregman, who signed with Chicago last offseason , also earned the honor for the second time in his career.

The Cubs were tied with the Toronto Blue Jays for the most Gold Glove nominees with five, though only Crow-Armstrong and Bregman ended up with wins. In an interview on the ESPN broadcast for the award, Bregman spoke about Chicago's commitment to defense.

"I know our team takes a lot of pride in defense, and it's pretty awesome to be on the field with a bunch of guys that care about the little details of the game," Bregman said.

The Milwaukee Brewers, coming off their World Series-winning run , had two players represented among the winners: left fielder Jackson Chourio and second baseman Brice Turang. Chourio, who had a shot at World Series MVP , earned his first Gold Glove award by beating out Chicago's Ian Happ, who had won the award for four straight seasons.

The best-represented teams were the Boston Red Sox and the Arizona Diamondbacks, who finished with three of the defensive awards each. Red Sox right fielder Wilyer Abreu took home his third straight Gold Glove after another dominant season.

There were some surprising snubs as well, though: Toronto, despite having five nominees, didn't take home any of the awards after a pretty mediocre season. Neither did the Kansas City Royals, whose four nominees included players like first baseman Vinnie Pasquantino and shortstop Bobby Witt Jr.

articles.title: Jerry Koosman, who got final out in the 1969 Miracle Mets’ World Series victory, dies
articles.summary: Jerry Koosman, an All-Star left-hander who got the final out of the Miracle Mets’ shocking 1969 World Series victory over the Baltimore Orioles, died Sunday.
articles.body: NEW YORK — Jerry Koosman, an All-Star left-hander who got the final out of the Miracle Mets’ shocking 1969 World Series victory over the Baltimore Orioles, died Sunday. He was 83. Mets spokesman Jay Horwitz said Koosman had been sick for about a year and died of multiple illnesses in Osceola, Wisconsin, surrounded by his children. Koosman jumping onto catcher Jerry Grote as they hugged on the Shea Stadium mound after the final out of the World Series remains an iconic image in baseball history. The Mets had never finished with a winning record before 1969. “We were so choked up with emotion we couldn’t talk,” Koosman was quoted as saying in Peter Golenbock’s 2002 book, “Amazin’: The Miraculous History of New York’s Most Beloved Baseball Team.” Koosman went 222-209 with a 3.36 ERA over 19 major league seasons, throwing 140 complete games that included 33 shutouts and becoming a two-time 20-game winner. Relying primarily on fastballs and curves, he was 140-137 with a 3.09 ERA for the Mets from 1967-78, then pitched for Minnesota (1979-81), the Chicago White Sox (1981-83) and Philadelphia (1984-85). “I feared losing. I didn’t want to be looked upon as a loser by anyone,” Koosman said in a 2019 interview with Mets broadcaster Howie Rose. An expansion franchise that launched in 1962, the Mets lost 100 games in five of their first seven seasons and had not come come close to a winning record. Then in 1969, they surged into first place on Sept. 10 during a 10-game winning streak, winning 38 of their last 49 games and finishing atop the new National League East with a 100-62 record. New York’s No. 2 starter behind future Hall of Famer Tom Seaver, Koosman went 17-9 with a 2.28 ERA in 32 starts in 1969. Koosman was knocked out in the fifth inning in Game 2 against Atlanta of the first NL Championship Series before the Mets rallied and went on to sweep the Braves in the best-of-five matchup. After Baltimore beat Seaver and the Mets 4-1 in the World Series opener, Koosman allowed one run over 8 2/3 innings and got the victory as New York won Game 2 by 2-1. Koosman pitched a five-hitter in Game 5, retiring future Mets manager Davey Johnson on a game-ending flyout to left fielder Cleon Jones as thousands of fans rushed onto the field at Shea Stadium. “I turn around and look at Cleon and I see Cleon going back and, uh, the first thing is the heart stops,” Koosman told Rose. “Well, then you see him slow down — oh, God, now you know it’s OK. Now the only other thing is: Don’t drop the ball.” Koosman was honored with a parade when he returned home to Morris, Minnesota. Born in Appleton, Minnesota, on Dec. 23, 1942, Koosman played baseball while with the U.S. Army at Fort Bragg in North Carolina. According to his biography by Irv Goldfarb of the Society for American Baseball Research, his catcher was John Luchese, son of a Shea Stadium usher. Luchese told his father about Koosman, who passed the information to Joe McDonald in the Mets’ front office. Koosman signed on Aug. 27, 1964, for $1,600. Koosman worked his way up the minor league system and made his big league debut on April 14, 1967, at Philadelphia’s Connie Mack Stadium with 2 2/3 hitless innings of relief. He was sent to Triple-A Jacksonville when rosters were trimmed and led the International League with 183 strikeouts. He made it to the major leagues for good in 1968, pitching a four-hit shutout at Dodger Stadium in his first start. He was picked for the All-Star team and faced one batter, striking out Carl Yastrzemski for the final out in the NL’s 1-0 win at Houston’s Astrodome. Koosman finished 19-12 with a 2.08 ERA on a staff led by Seaver that included a young Nolan Ryan. He finished second to Cincinnati catcher Johnny Bench in NL Rookie of the year voting He was part of the 1969 rotation with Seaver, Gary Gentry, Don Cardwell and Jim McAndruw, again making the All-Star team. “There’s the old saying: good pitching gets out good hitting,” Koosman when the Mets retired his No. 36 in 2021. “So that’s what happened and our pitching kind of took over.” With the Mets trailing 3-0 in the sixth inning of Game 5 against the Orioles, Cleon Jones claimed a Dave McNally pitch hit him. The ball bounced to Koosman, seated in the Mets dugout by manager Gil Hodges. “As I bent down, Gil says: ‘Swipe it against your shoe,’” Koosman told Rose. Hodges then showed the ball to plate umpire Lou DiMuro, who awarded Jones first base. Donn Clendenon followed with a two-run homer, starting the Mets’ comeback in a 5-3. “Maybe it wasn’t mine. Maybe it was Cleon’s show polish,” Koosman said. He made two starts in the 1973 World Series against Oakland, getting no decision in Game 2 and winning Game 5. With the Mets in decline, Koosman told the team after the 1978 season he would retire unless traded. The Mets dealt him to the Twins in December 1978, and he later was traded to the White Sox in August 1981 and to the Phillies in February 1984. He is survived by sons Michael and Shawn, and daughter Danielle. His marriage to the former LaVonne Sorum ended in a divorce.

articles.title: MLB ‘spot-fixing’ trial set to begin in US court
articles.summary: MLB pitchers charged with conspiracy to influence sporting contests by bribery go on trial in New York.
articles.body:
Former Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz go on trial on Monday on charges of accepting bribes after colluding with gamblers who made hundreds of thousands of dollars by betting correctly on individual pitches in Major League Baseball (MLB) in the United States.

Their careers and possibly their freedom are at stake in the jury trial expected to unfold over the next month in New York’s Brooklyn federal court. Several professional baseball players, including catchers and baseball executives, are among witnesses expected to testify.

Clase, the Guardians’ former closer, and Ortiz, a starter, have pleaded not guilty to conspiracy charges and are on non-disciplinary leave from the club without pay while their fate is determined.

According to an indictment, the pitchers accepted thousands of dollars in payoffs to help two gamblers from their native Dominican Republic win at least $460,000 on in-game prop bets on the speed and outcome of certain pitches.

Prosecutors allege that Clase began providing the betters with information about his pitches in 2023 and recruited Ortiz into the scheme in 2025. Ortiz’s lawyers unsuccessfully sought to have him tried separately from Clase.

Judge Kiyo A Matsumoto said at a conference last Friday that she hopes to complete jury selection quickly enough that lawyers can deliver relatively short opening statements in the afternoon.

Clase, 28, is a three-time All-Star and two-time American League Reliever of the Year who had completed his fourth season of a $20m, five-year contract when charges against the pitchers were revealed in November 2025.

Ortiz, 27, had earned $782,600 as a starting pitcher for the Guardians during the 2025 season.

The pitchers have been charged with wire fraud conspiracy, honest services wire fraud conspiracy, money laundering conspiracy and conspiracy to influence sporting contests by bribery.

Defence lawyers are expected to argue that the pitchers did not collude with gamblers and instead were varying the placement of pitches strategically to fool batters.

On Friday, the judge ruled that prosecutors cannot show the jury proof that Clase owed $500,000 in US taxes because they had only provided the evidence to defence lawyers several days earlier and long after a deadline had passed to turn over evidence to their adversaries.

A prosecutor had argued that the government wanted to put the evidence in the trial to offset any claim by Clase’s lawyers that he had no incentive to collude with gamblers because he had several million dollars in financial accounts in the Dominican Republic.

MLB and the Guardians have said they have fully cooperated with authorities. MLB said it contacted federal law enforcement when it began investigating unusual betting activity.

articles.title: Picking Every MLB Team's MVP, Cy Young and Rookie of the Year in 2026
articles.summary: Before the baseball world fully shifts focus to the offseason, let's slap a bow on the 2026 campaign by selecting the MVP, Cy Young and Rookie of the Year for every MLB team.
articles.body:
Before the baseball world fully shifts focus to the offseason, let's slap a bow on the 2026 campaign by selecting the MVP, Cy Young and Rookie of the Year for every MLB team.

There is little drama with the leaguewide awards this year. Pete Crow-Armstrong and Yordan Alvarez are the MVP favorites, Jacob Misiorowski and Cam Schlittler could both win their respective Cy Young Awards unanimously, and Kevin McGonigle is a lock for AL Rookie of the Year honors. The only real debate is the NL Rookie of the Year race.

However, zooming in on the top candidate for each award on a team level creates a more compelling conversation.

Only position players were considered for the team MVP award, while rookies were eligible to also be selected as their team's MVP or Cy Young. Just like the actual leaguewide awards, the focus was also solely on regular-season production.

ARI | ATH | ATL | BAL | BOS | CHC | CIN | CLE | COL | CWS | DET | HOU | KC | LAA | LAD | MIA | MIL | MIN | NYM | NYY | PHI | PIT | SD | SEA | SF | STL | TB | TEX | TOR | WSH

MVP: C Gabriel Moreno Cy Young: SP Eduardo Rodríguez ROY: RP Brandyn Garcia

Just the fifth catcher in MLB history to win a batting title, Gabriel Moreno hit .311/.388/.486 for a 143 OPS+ with 33 doubles, 16 home runs, 83 RBI and an impressive 6.7 WAR in 130 games.

In the third season of a four-year, $80 million deal that saw him log a 5.02 ERA in 204.1 innings over the first two seasons, Eduardo Rodríguez earned his first All-Star selection. The 33-year-old went 16-7 with a 2.89 ERA in 189.2 innings.

MVP: 1B Nick Kurtz Cy Young: SP J.T. Ginn ROY: OF Henry Bolte

The Athletics had a variety of injuries up and down the roster, including to MVP pick Nick Kurtz , though he still managed a 141 OPS+ with 21 home runs and 3.7 WAR in 99 games.

Those injuries opened the door for top prospect Henry Bolte to carve out an everyday role, and he hit .277/.359/.405 for a 110 OPS+ while also logging strong defensive metrics (5 DRS, 5 OAA) en route to a 3.3-WAR debut.

MVP: OF Michael Harris II Cy Young: SP Chris Sale ROY: RP Didier Fuentes

A runner-up finish in NL Cy Young balloting likely awaits Chris Sale , who continues to put up some of the best numbers of his career in his late 30s, going 14-9 with a 2.16 ERA, 0.98 WHIP and 200 strikeouts in 162.2 innings.

The MVP debate is a compelling one between Michael Harris II (121 OPS+, 63 XBH, 26 HR, 5.1 WAR) and Matt Olson (123 OPS+, 75 XBH, 41 HR, 4.4 WAR), and the edge goes to Harris thanks to his standout defense (9 DRS, 13 OAA) at a premium position.

Predicting Early Signings in Free Agency 🔮

MVP: 1B Pete Alonso Cy Young: SP Trevor Rogers ROY: C/DH Samuel Basallo

The Orioles inked Pete Alonso to a five-year, $155 million deal last offseason, and it ended up being one of the best moves of the winter as he went on to log a 149 OPS+ while leading the AL in home runs (43) and RBI (113).

With Adley Rutschman traded at the deadline, Samuel Basallo (112 G, 29 XBH, 18 HR, 1.6 WAR) is now the present and future at the catcher position. He is still only 22 years old, and locked up with an eight-year extension that runs all the way through the 2033 campaign.

MVP: 1B Willson Contreras Cy Young: SP Sonny Gray ROY: SP Payton Tolle

The Red Sox traded Hunter Dobbins, Richard Fitts and three prospects to acquire Willson Contreras (153 OPS+, 51 XBH, 27 HR, 4.6 WAR) and Sonny Gray (18-5, 2.72 ERA, 1.15 WHIP, 169.0 IP, 4.3 WAR) in separate trades with the Cardinals during the offseason, and they ended up being arguably the two most productive players on the roster.

A strong season from Gray helped offset an injury-plagued season from Garrett Crochet, but a fantastic rookie campaign from Payton Tolle (9-6, 3.03 ERA, 1.10 WHIP, 171 K, 148.2 IP) also went a long way as he settled in as the No. 2 arm on the staff.

Pete Crow-Armstrong was MLB's WAR leader with a 9.8-WAR campaign that included 45 home runs, 41 steals, an NL-leading 156 OPS+ and Gold Glove-caliber defense (16 DRS, 25 OAA) in center field.

In a revolving door starting rotation, Shota Imanaga started 32 games and logged a 3.77 ERA, 1.10 WHIP and 174 strikeouts in 174.1 innings. He was the only pitcher on the roster to surpass 140 innings of work, and his 14 quality starts were five more than anyone else on the staff.

MVP: 3B Miguel Vargas Cy Young: SP Sean Burke ROY: OF Tristan Peters

There is a case to be made that Munetaka Murakami (130 OPS+, 35 HR, 2.3 WAR) could be the pick for MVP and Rookie of the Year, but his loud rookie campaign was ultimately outpaced by fellow All-Star selections Miguel Vargas (134 OPS+, 33 HR, 22 SB, 5.4 WAR) and Tristan Peters (116 OPS+, 47 XBH, 3.6 WAR).

Right-hander Sean Burke (11-7, 3.34 ERA, 1.20 WHIP, 185 K, 172.1 IP) was the clear ace of the staff, though multi-inning relievers Grant Taylor and Sean Newcomb at least deserve a mention for their work filling a variety of roles on the staff.

MVP: SS Elly De La Cruz Cy Young: SP Chase Burns ROY: IF Sal Stewart

Along with the first 30/30 season of his career, Elly De La Cruz also showed a more complete secondary game with a career-high .365 on-base percentage and more consistent defense at shortstop.

The Reds were careful to manage workload with Chase Burns , as he completed six innings in just 12 of his 29 starts, but he finished 15-3 with a 2.86 ERA, 1.17 WHIP and 185 strikeouts in 154.1 innings. The 23-year-old effectively filled the role of staff ace with Hunter Greene sidelined.

MVP: OF Chase DeLauter Cy Young: SP Parker Messick ROY: SP Parker Messick

There is a debate to be had between Parker Messick (12-9, 2.56 ERA, 1.06 WHIP, 193 K, 186.1 IP, 6.3 WAR) and Gavin Williams (14-8, 3.76 ERA, 1.11 WHIP, 248 K, 184.1 IP, 3.1 WAR) for Cleveland's Cy Young honors, though Messick's ERA is difficult to ignore.

With José Ramírez struggling through a down year while navigating a fractured hamate bone in his left hand, Chase DeLauter anchored Cleveland's offense. The rookie outfielder hit .287/.363/.457 for a 131 OPS+ with 30 doubles, 16 home runs, 67 RBI and a team-high 226 total bases.

MVP: C Hunter Goodman Cy Young: SP Tomoyuki Sugano ROY: 1B TJ Rumfield

An All-Star for the second straight season, Hunter Goodman posted a 115 OPS+ and slugged 41 home runs to finish behind only Pete Crow-Armstrong (45) and Kyle Schwarber (45) on the NL leaderboard.

Rookie TJ Rumfield was acquired in an under-the-radar deal with the Yankees last offseason, and he hit .300 with an NL-leading .390 on-base percentage after staking his claim to Colorado's primary first base job. The 26-year-old now looks like a cost-controlled building block for the Rockies.

MVP: SS/3B Kevin McGonigle Cy Young: SP Keider Montero ROY: SS/3B Kevin McGonigle

Not only did Kevin McGonigle pace all rookies with his 7.1-WAR season, but that gaudy total trailed only Pete Crow-Armstrong (9.8), Cristopher Sánchez (8.1) and Brice Turang (7.3) among all players across baseball.

With Tarik Skubal and Casey Mize both traded at the deadline and Framber Valdez putting together a lackluster debut in Detroit, the Cy Young debate came down to Keider Montero (10-9, 3.48 ERA, 1.04 WHIP, 107 K, 155.0 IP) and Troy Melton (8-5, 2.76 ERA, 1.13 WHIP, 94 K, 114.1 IP). Both will be counted on to be key pieces of the rotation in 2027.

MVP: DH Yordan Alvarez Cy Young: SP Peter Lambert ROY: RP AJ Blubaugh

Yordan Alvarez made a legitimate run at AL Triple Crown honors, ultimately settling for the batting title (.316 BA) and runner-up finishes in home runs (42) and RBI (106) in a season that should end in AL MVP honors.

A tip of the cap to Peter Lambert for leading the team in innings pitched (155.2), strikeouts (154) and pitching WAR (3.1), helping to prop up an injury-plagued staff. Rookie AJ Blubaugh also finished third on the team with 96 innings, despite pitching exclusively in relief, posting a 3.66 ERA in 64 appearances.

Even with just 18 home runs, Bobby Witt Jr. still had a solid case for best all-around shortstop in baseball. He posted a 125 OPS+ with 52 extra-base hits, 45 steals and 6.7 WAR while again playing Gold Glove-caliber defense.

Rookie Carter Jensen led the team in home runs (27) and RBI (81), and he had an .882 OPS with 14 long balls in 60 games after the All-Star break. Expected to be the primary DH and backup catcher when the season began, he also ended up starting 97 games behind the plate.

MVP: SS Zach Neto Cy Young: SP Reid Detmers ROY: SP Walbert Ureña

With three straight 5-WAR seasons, Zach Neto stands as one of baseball's most underrated stars. The 25-year-old recorded his third straight 20/20 campaign with a career-high 27 home runs and 24 steals while posting a 118 OPS+ as one of the few offensive standouts in the Angels' lineup.

Reid Detmers (7-8, 3.36 ERA, 1.04 WHIP, 211 K, 185.0 IP) emerged as the ace of the staff in his return to a starting role, while Walbert Ureña (9-11, 2.97 ERA, 1.23 WHIP, 142 K, 148.1 IP) broke out to help make the deadline trade of José Soriano easier to justify.

MVP: OF Andy Pages Cy Young: SP Yoshinobu Yamamoto ROY: IF Alex Freeland

On a roster loaded with star power, Andy Pages led all position players with 6.0 WAR and carried the offense for stretches. The 25-year-old had a 122 OPS+ with 23 home runs and 85 RBI while also playing stellar defense (20 DRS, 9 OAA) in center field en route to being a Gold Glove finalist.

Infielder Alex Freeland hit a respectable .234/.327/.325 with 13 extra-base hits and 1.1 WAR in 89 games as the Dodgers' most impactful rookie. Shoutout to Josue De Paula for his .323/.500/.581 line over 42 plate appearances filling in at DH for Shohei Ohtani down the stretch.

MVP: SS Otto Lopez Cy Young: SP Sandy Alcantara ROY: C Joe Mack

There has not been a quieter 6-WAR season in recent memory than the year Otto Lopez just put together, as he hit .305/.349/.437 for a 122 OPS+ while racking up an NL-leading 191 hits and playing standout defense at shortstop.

He might not have returned to Cy Young form, but Sandy Alcantara provided plenty of value as a workhorse, leading the NL in innings pitched (214.0) while logging a 3.87 ERA and 104 ERA+ atop the Miami staff.

There is certainly a case to be made that William Contreras is the most irreplaceable player on the Milwaukee roster, but there's no ignoring a 7.3-WAR season from Brice Turang . He posted a 124 OPS+ with 37 doubles, 21 home runs, 100 RBI and 19 steals, and he won his second career Gold Glove at second base.

Jacob Misiorowski 's rise to frontline ace and NL Cy Young favorite was one of the biggest storylines of the year for the Brewers, but Logan Henderson deserves a ton of credit for stabilizing the rotation behind him. The rookie right-hander did not allow more than three earned runs in any of his 18 starts, finishing with a 2.47 ERA and 0.84 WHIP in 98.1 innings.

MVP: IF/OF Kody Clemens Cy Young: SP Taj Bradley ROY: SP Connor Prielipp

How many people outside of the state of Minnesota know that Kody Clemens led the Twins with 27 home runs this season? He posted a 109 OPS+ and 2.7 WAR over 145 games, and he split his time between first base, second base and the outfield.

The move to buy low on Taj Bradley in exchange for Griffin Jax at the 2025 trade deadline paid major dividends this year, as he broke through as the ace of the staff. Still only 25 years old, he had a 3.73 ERA and 205 strikeouts in 178.1 innings over 31 starts.

MVP: OF Carson Benge Cy Young: SP Nolan McLean ROY: SP Nolan McLean

For all the money the Mets spent trying to field a competitive roster, rookies Nolan McLean (12-10, 3.16 ERA, 1.17 WHIP, 194 K, 179.2 IP) and Carson Benge (118 OPS+, 20 HR, 22 SB, 4.3 WAR) ended up being their best players over the course of the entire 2026 season.

Juan Soto had an elite 154 OPS+, but he played just 111 games, making it tougher to hand him team MVP honors. It will be interesting to see where McLean and Benge fall in NL Rookie of the Year balloting, though both seem to be chasing Cincinnati's Sal Stewart.

MVP: DH Ben Rice Cy Young: SP Cam Schlittler ROY: OF Spencer Jones

With Aaron Judge limited to 66 games and Gerrit Cole and Carlos Rodón both sidelined to start the year, the Yankees leaned hard on breakout seasons from Ben Rice and Cam Schlittler .

Rice had a 146 OPS+ with 41 home runs and 97 RBI in a season where no other Yankees player reached 20 long balls, while Schlittler is the heavy favorite for AL Cy Young honors after he went 14-6 with a 1.95 ERA, 0.92 WHIP and 239 strikeouts in 193.2 innings.

With a 128 OPS+ and 45 home runs, tied for the NL lead, Kyle Schwarber was again one of the game's most productive offensive players. Left-hander Cristopher Sánchez helped pick up the slack while Zack Wheeler missed time, and he looked like the NL Cy Young favorite during the first half while rattling off a 50.2-inning scoreless streak.

Right-hander Andrew Painter (23 GS, 5.40 ERA, 115 K, 126.2 IP, 1.3 WAR) and center fielder Justin Crawford (149 G, 78 OPS+, 27 XBH, 17 SB, -0.2 WAR) both made the Opening Day roster and filled key roles throughout the year, though neither finished with a standout individual stat line.

MVP: 2B Brandon Lowe Cy Young: SP Braxton Ashcraft ROY: OF Esmerlyn Valdez

The Pirates' trade to acquire Brandon Lowe (121 OPS+, 35 HR, 96 RBI) ended up being one of the best moves of the offseason, helping to transform what was baseball's worst offense in 2025 into a vastly improved group.

Braxton Ashcraft (28 GS, 3.65 ERA, 1.09 WHIP, 173 K, 165.1 IP, 3.5 WAR) ended up outperforming Paul Skenes (32 GS, 3.82 ERA, 1.12 WHIP, 200 K, 174.1 IP, 3.3 WAR) atop the Pittsburgh rotation, which is indicative of both Ashcraft's breakout and Skenes' regression.

MVP: OF Fernando Tatis Jr. Cy Young: RP Mason Miller ROY: RP Bradgley Rodríguez

After a rocky start to the season, Fernando Tatis Jr. hit .307/.385/.610 with 20 home runs in 64 games after the All-Star break, and a red-hot final two months helped lead the Padres back into the playoff picture.

Ace Michael King (32 GS, 12-10, 3.21 ERA, 1.18 WHIP, 159 K, 185.0 IP, 4.3 WAR) and closer Mason Miller (66 G, 38 SV, 1.67 ERA, 16.6 K/9, 3.1 WAR) both have a solid case for team Cy Young honors. The best relief pitcher in baseball gets the nod here, and it will be interesting to see if he hits the trade block this winter.

MVP: 1B Rafael Devers Cy Young: SP Logan Webb ROY: DH Bryce Eldridge

The one-two punch of Rafael Devers (142 OPS+, 37 HR, 98 RBI, 3.6 WAR) and Bryce Eldridge (133 OPS+, 17 HR, 57 RBI, 2.1 WAR) has a chance to be the best power-hitting tandem to share the San Francisco lineup since Barry Bonds and Jeff Kent were teammates.

Even in a down year by his standards, Logan Webb was still an All-Star, finishing with a 4.31 ERA, 1.17 WHIP and 134 strikeouts in 160.2 innings. He was slowed by knee bursitis earlier in the year and shut down early with a blister issue.

MVP: OF Randy Arozarena Cy Young: SP Logan Gilbert ROY: SP Kade Anderson

With a career-high 148 OPS+ and a sixth straight 20/20 season, Randy Arozarena enters free agency for the first time in his career as the most impactful bat on this year's offseason market. The 31-year-old had an excellent .381 on-base percentage and scored an AL-leading 113 runs.

Just a year removed from pitching LSU to a College World Series title and going No. 3 overall in the 2025 draft, Kade Anderson looked right at home in the big leagues after an utterly dominant run through the minors. The 22-year-old had a 3.79 ERA, 1.23 WHIP and 32 strikeouts in 35.2 innings over seven starts after debuting on Aug. 22.

MVP: 1B Alec Burleson Cy Young: SP Michael McGreevy ROY: 2B JJ Wetherholt

While Jordan Walker (124 OPS+, 62 XBH, 29 HR, 102 RBI, 3.3 WAR) received significant attention for his breakthrough performance, fellow slugger Alec Burleson (131 OPS+, 64 XBH, 26 HR, 116 RBI, 3.7 WAR) ended up having the better overall season.

The Cardinals have assembled a solid offensive core, but there is significant work to be done on the pitching side of things. Michael McGreevy , Andre Pallante and Kyle Leahy put up similar numbers, and McGreevy gets the Cy Young nod on the strength of his team-high 168.2 innings of work.

MVP: 3B Junior Caminero Cy Young: SP Drew Rasmussen ROY: OF Victor Mesa Jr.

With a second straight 40-homer, 100-RBI season, Junior Caminero has firmly established himself as one of the game's elite sluggers, and he won't turn 24 years old until midway through the 2027 season. If anyone is going to steal first-place votes from Yordan Alvarez on the AL MVP ballot, it's him.

Acquired from the Marlins in an under-the-radar offseason deal, Victor Mesa Jr. emerged as Tampa Bay's primary right fielder during the second half of the season. He hit .288/.338/.555 with 18 extra-base hits in 158 plate appearances after the All-Star break, and is controllable through 2031.

MVP: IF/OF Ezequiel Durán Cy Young: RP Jacob Latz ROY: RP Peyton Gray

The Rangers bullpen looked like a glaring hole heading into the season, but starter-turned-closer Jacob Latz (58 G, 30 SV, 2.13 ERA, 0.81 WHIP, 10.4 K/9) and 31-year-old rookie Peyton Gray (49 G, 8 HLD, 3.86 ERA, 9.6 K/9) ended up being key cogs in a strong relief corps.

With 25 or more starts at second base, shortstop and third base, along with some sporadic action in the outfield, Ezequiel Durán was baseball's best utility player. The 27-year-old had a 114 OPS+ and 4.2 WAR in 153 games while bouncing around the field.

MVP: 3B Kazuma Okamoto Cy Young: SP Dylan Cease ROY: 3B Kazuma Okamoto

The Blue Jays signed Kazuma Okamoto to a four-year, $60 million deal, and he finished as the team leader in home runs (33), RBI (92) and OPS+ (107) during his first season. He also played a rock-solid third base after some thought he might be limited to first base stateside.

The seven-year, $210 million contract given to Dylan Cease was a significantly larger financial investment, and he could end up as the AL Cy Young runner-up. He made his long-overdue first All-Star Game and finished with a 2.40 ERA and 239 strikeouts in 169 innings.

MVP: SS CJ Abrams Cy Young: SP Cade Cavalli ROY: SP Foster Griffin

The CJ Abrams (127 OPS+, 33 HR, 106 RBI, 34 SB, 5.1 WAR) vs. James Wood (144 OPS+, 30 HR, 77 RBI, 21 SB, 3.7 WAR) debate for team MVP honors is a good snapshot of why the Nationals had one of the highest-scoring offenses in baseball, and assuming both players stay put this winter, they can again make the lineup a strength.

A finally healthy Cade Cavalli (13-5, 3.02 ERA, 1.16 WHIP, 200 K, 169.2 IP) emerged as the ace of the staff following the offseason trade of MacKenzie Gore to the Rangers. He was rewarded with a four-year, $47 million extension in September.

articles.title: Educated Guesses On MLB Free Agency 2026 Early Signings
articles.summary: With a lockout looming on Dec. 2, MLB free agents and teams alike are facing a difficult question: Now or later?
articles.body:
With a lockout looming on Dec. 2, MLB free agents and teams alike are facing a difficult question: Now or later?

When the most recent lockout happened during the 2021-22 offseason, the camps were split pretty much right down the middle. Of the 11 players who signed for at least $100M that winter, six did so in the last 2-3 days before the lockout began, while the other five waited out the storm and signed in mid/late March.

Back then, though, adding a salary cap was more of a pipe dream for owners than the current "come hell or high water" stance that they seemingly have on the matter.

So, will there be more or less of a last-minute frenzy of signings on Nov. 30 and Dec. 1?

The hunch is that Tarik Skubal signs early, to ensure that what will be a monstrous contract gets locked in before the sport's financial structure potentially gets shaken to its very core. But aside from him, teams might be content to wait and see what happens.

In particular, it's probably going to be a quiet month for players who are strong candidates for three- to five-year contracts but are already in their early 30s—i.e., Randy Arozarena, Ian Happ, Seiya Suzuki, etc.—given the threat (regardless of how credible you believe it to be) of the entire 2027 season getting canceled.

But, hey, let's make some guesses at signings that will happen in the next month.

Tyler Mahle was maybe the greatest under-the-radar trade deadline acquisition of all time. Between the regular season and postseason, he made 11 starts for the Atlanta Braves with a 1.86 ERA.

All told, nine of his 11 appearances with Atlanta were quality starts. In fact, he and Tampa Bay's Drew Rasmussen were the only pitchers to make multiple quality starts in the postseason, this despite Mahle making just two appearances to Rasmussen's five.

Not bad for a guy who had a 5.13 ERA through his 18 starts with San Francisco.

And, well, Atlanta could really use him back.

After the past couple of years, banking on either Spencer Strider or Reynaldo López staying healthy seems to be a fool's errand. If and when Spencer Schwellenbach will return after missing the entire 2026 season and undergoing elbow surgery two months ago is a big unknown. And though Didier Fuentes had a fantastic season out of the bullpen, can they stretch him out to be an effective starter in 2027?

Aside from Chris Sale, lots of question marks.

But re-upping with Mahle on a one-year, $20M or two-year, $37M type of contract could be a match made in heaven.

Teruaki Sato Signs with New York Yankees

Five years ago, Seiya Suzuki was posted by his Nippon Professional Baseball club on November 22, opening a 45-day window in which he could sign with an MLB team.

He signed with the Cubs 116 days later, which was possible because the clock on his posting window was paused during the 99-day lockout.

It is our understanding that Teruaki Sato would be in the same boat if he is unable to finalize a deal before the lockout begins, and that he doesn't necessarily need to sign within the next month.

However, the expectation is that Sato will officially be posted this week (possibly even today), and that teams will be particularly motivated to sign him ASAP. Because if he's not signed by Dec. 2 and the lockout seriously threatens to postpone the start of—or cancel altogether—the 2027 season, there's probably going to come a point where he simply returns to the Hanshin Tigers with plans to reenter free agency in 2029.

Long story short, get ready for Sato to sign somewhere in the coming weeks.

And now that we know Bo Bichette will return to the New York Mets for another $42M season in 2027, it might be the other New York team that makes the winning bid for Sato.

There are major question marks about his ability to play third base in the majors. Since the beginning of 2023, he has committed 73 errors in his 1,226 chances at the hot corner. That's a .940 fielding percentage, which is kind of awful.

Then again, Kazuma Okamoto had a .935 fielding percentage for the Blue Jays this season, and no one was complaining about his impact with 33 home runs. Same goes for Junior Caminero's career .945 fielding percentage at third base while he racked up 87 home runs and 211 RBI over the past two years.

If Sato's bat (79 home runs and 208 RBI over the past two seasons) translates to the majors as well as that of Okamoto and Munetaka Murakami did, the Yankees would gladly live with 25-30 errors at third base in exchange for a much greater offensive impact than Ryan McMahon has provided.

Washington Nationals Make a Big Splash in Starting Pitcher Market

For all the forthcoming talk of a salary cap, the Washington Nationals might want to start planning for a salary floor.

(And, you know, trying to improve the team so they can contend for a change in 2027.)

As things stand, they owe Keibert Ruiz $5M next year and Cade Cavalli $4M—and those are their only known figures at the moment.

While CJ Abrams is probably going to get $10M-$11M in what will be his next-to-last year of arbitration eligibility, he's probably the only other player already on this roster who is going to make at least $3M in 2027.

Despite that infinitesimal payroll, the Nationals could be a contender if they adequately address their pitching shortcomings.

They traded for Connelly Early, but he made just one appearance for them late in the season. He should be a middle-of-the-rotation guy in 2027. They also got both Josiah Gray and DJ Herz back from Tommy John surgeries in September, either of whom could be a tantalizing back-of-the-rotation option next to Andrew Alvarez.

Put a Freddy Peralta, Trevor Rogers or Michael King type of arm atop the rotation alongside Cavalli and this team's outlook drastically changes for the better.

And of the three, King might be the best bet to sign with the Nationals, considering he is the eldest of the bunch and could be a much-needed veteran presence in that rotation/clubhouse.

At any rate, if he doesn't re-sign with San Diego, Washington makes as much sense as any landing spot. And after going through free agency last winter and already declining his player option for 2027, he might be in more of a rush than most to get a deal done ahead of the lockout.

On Monday evening, we will officially find out which free agents received qualifying offers. It's very likely that Brandon Lowe will be on that relatively short list of names.

It's also likely that the 32-year-old second baseman will decline that one-year, $23.15M offer in pursuit of a multi-year deal.

However, that doesn't necessarily mean the relationship between Lowe and Pittsburgh is finished.

If anything, it's practically an annual tradition at this point that multiple players will decline a qualifying offer before ultimately re-signing with the same team.

Kyle Schwarber, Michael King and Zac Gallen all fit the bill this past winter. Same goes for Pete Alonso, Teoscar Hernández and Sean Manaea the previous offseason. There were two such players (Aaron Nola and Cody Bellinger) during the 2023-24 offseason, three (Aaron Judge, Brandon Nimmo and Anthony Rizzo) in 2022-23 and three more (Raisel Iglesias, Chris Taylor and Justin Verlander) in 2021-22.

So why not Lowe, who was Pittsburgh's MVP with 35 home runs and 96 RBI in 2026?

If the Pirates let him get away, second base becomes a major problem for them. (Or third base, if they move Nick Gonzales from the hot corner back to his previous home.) Either way, as the roster presently stands, they'd be forced to play one of Jared Triolo, Jacob Gonzalez, Nick Yorke or Tyler Callihan on a daily basis, and they had a collective OPS of around .610 this past season.

Help should eventually be coming in the form of Murf Gray. The third baseman had 32 home runs and a .969 OPS in 126 games played in the minors in 2026, but he might still be a year away.

In the meantime, bringing back Lowe on a short-term deal would be fantastic for a team that is in "win now" mode for the first time in a decade.

What happens when you combine the best ground ball pitcher in the sport (Clay Holmes) with the most home run-averse stadium in the country (Oracle Park in San Francisco)?

Dating back to 2019, Holmes has logged 17.2 innings pitched at Oracle Park, allowing just one run (no home runs). And if the Giants make a good enough offer in the coming weeks, perhaps we'll get to find out what that looks like over a much larger sample size.

Holmes has a 62.7 percent ground ball rate since the beginning of 2021. Among pitchers who have logged at least 400 innings during that window, the only others at 59 percent or greater are Andre Pallante (61.6) and Framber Valdez (60.5).

Holmes' 0.56 HR/9 rate over the past six seasons is also the lowest among all pitchers with at least 400 innings of work, tied with Tyler Rogers and slightly ahead of Logan Webb in third place, both of whom have already benefited from life at Oracle Park, where home runs go to die.

And beyond the ground ball rate, Holmes is exactly the kind of relatively affordable veteran No. 2 or No. 3 starter the Giants always seem to target. They'll probably need to spend a bit more than usual to secure the former closer turned starter who turns 34 in March, but they should be able to afford a three-year, $63M type of deal to help fill out what is presently looking like a much less than stellar rotation for 2027.

Mauricio Dubón to the Los Angeles Dodgers

Compared to the massive contracts inked with Freddie Freeman, Shohei Ohtani, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Kyle Tucker in recent years, Mauricio Dubón signing with the Los Angeles Dodgers wouldn't even register on the "MLB fans' outrage" Richter scale.

But between Miguel Rojas retiring and Kiké Hernández hitting free agency, the Dodgers have a need for an established asset who can play virtually anywhere. At any rate, Freddie Freeman is 37, Max Muncy is 36, and Mookie Betts and Teoscar Hernández are both 34. Planning on them playing in a combined total of anywhere close to 600 games in 2027 would certainly be a decision.

The big unknown with Dubón is whether he'd prefer to remain in a super-sub role or if he's looking for a spot where he would serve as the team's primary (insert position here).

If it's the latter, maybe he can become LA's primary second baseman? That spot in the lineup has been a revolving door over the past two years.

If it's the former, he'd be a welcome addition to just about any roster—especially if Jim Bowden's projection of two years, $16M is an accurate representation of Dubón's cost in free agency. But the Dodgers, in particular, have shown an affinity for guys who can play anywhere and everywhere.

Pair him with the also versatile Tommy Edman and the Dodgers' depth chart is pretty much set.

Tarik Skubal is presently the greatest pitcher in baseball. Anyone who tries to tell you otherwise is only fooling themselves.

Despite missing six weeks after undergoing arthroscopic "Skubal Scope" surgery on his elbow, he had a 2.70 ERA before the procedure and a 2.73 ERA after it, thriving regardless of whether he was pitching for the Tigers or Dodgers. And that dominant run was actually a little worse than the standard he established while winning back-to-back AL Cy Young awards.

He turns 30 on Nov. 20, and what a fitting birthday gift it would be for him to sign the most lucrative contract for a pitcher (excluding Shohei Ohtani) on that very day.

The current record belongs to Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who signed his 12-year, $325M deal with the Dodgers three winters ago.

But both Skubal and the New York Mets will be motivated to break that record before the lockout.

As far as the exact numbers are concerned, who knows?

Some have speculated the total face value of Skubal's deal could be as high as $500M. I'm inclined to believe it'll be more in the eight years, $350M type of range, which would still break both the AAV record (that'd be $43.75M and the current record is $43.33M) and the total contract record for a pitcher.

Either way, it'll be a lot—an amount that perhaps only Steve Cohen can justify committing to at this point in time.

At any rate, if it isn't the Mets, the other logical suitor at this price point is the Dodgers. And if the Dodgers land him just before a potential lockout, their spending would likely become an even bigger flashpoint for frustrated fans.

articles.title: Astros Target Yankees Coach for Manager, Latest Update on Search for Vacant Job
articles.summary: The Houston Astros are interviewing Brad Ausmus as part of their managerial search, according to the New York Post's Jon Heyman.
articles.body:
The Houston Astros are interviewing Brad Ausmus as part of their managerial search, according to the New York Post 's Jon Heyman .

Ausmus, who's currently the New York Yankees bench coach, has a .486 winning percentage across his five seasons as an MLB manager. He was with the Detroit Tigers from 2014-17 and then led the Los Angeles Angels in 2019.

Last week, Houston tabbed Randy Flores as its next general manager. With that role filled, the organization will begin to focus more seriously on replacing Joe Espada.

Beyond his experience in the dugout, Ausmus had an 18-year playing career and was with the Astros for a decade.

In a lot of cases, hiring a longtime former player as the manager is an easy way to engender fan goodwill straight out of the gate. Appointing Ausmus could have the opposite effect in Houston, however.

Hall of Famer Jeff Bagwell is the senior advisor to ownership and baseball operations, and there's a general sense he's an influential voice behind the scenes. The Astros legend has made it no secret in the past he diverges a bit from the front office's old orthodoxy, one that resulted in two World Series titles.

The Athletic's Chandler Rome reported in June 2024 there were questions over how much authority GM Dana Brown wielded over personnel moves.

Were Ausmus to be the ultimate choice, it would further reinforce the perception that Bagwell has the ear of team owner Jim Crane.

Ausmus' track record isn't inspiring, either, as his lone playoff trip as a manager resulted in an ALDS sweep in 2014.

Only days removed from Flores' arrival, the Astros aren't on the verge of hiring their next manager. The process will continue to unfold in the coming days and perhaps weeks.

Ausmus won't be the last candidate seriously linked with the job.

articles.title: MLB sets Dec. 1 deadline for Japanese stars to sign before potential lockout
articles.summary: MLB will not extend the posting window for Japanese players, leaving Teruaki Sato and others facing a Dec. 1 deadline to sign.
articles.body:
Major League Baseball has angered the Major League Baseball Players Association and agents by informing them that will they not amend the posting agreement with Nippon Professional Baseball, requiring Japanese free agents to sign by the expected Dec. 1 lockout or they would be ineligible to sign with an MLB team in 2027.

The union sent a memo to agents last week, obtained by USA TODAY Sports, that said MLB on Tuesday denied their request, which was made in August, to extend the tolling period in the NPB posting agreement allowing posted players to sign after the lockout ended. This is direct contrast to the 99-day lockout in 2021 when MLB amended the 45-day negotiating window, and allowed Japanese free agents to sign after the lockout.

MLB confirmed Monday it is not amending its posting agreement.

The MLBPA said it is exploring its options, but informed agents last week to be prepared for a strict deadline for posted players.

This means that the three Japanese players who were posted Sunday, featuring prized infielder Teruaki Sato of the Hanshin Tigers, must sign by Dec. 1 if there's a lockout, instead of the traditional 45-day window. The other two posted players are pitchers Kaima Taira of the Seibu Lions and Hiromi Itoh of the Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters.

The extended window in 2021 for posted players allowed outfielder Seiya Suzuki to sign a five-year, $85 million contract with the Chicago Cubs eight days after the March 10 lockout ended.

Now, Japanese posted players will have less than 30 days to work out a deal.

While all free agents will be permitted to negotiate with all 30 teams beginning at 5 p.m. ET Monday, MLB players who are unsigned before the collective bargaining agreement ends on Dec. 1, still are eligible to sign once the lockout ends.

articles.title: Fraud Trial Underway in New York for Cleveland Guardians Pitchers, Including Star Reliever
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz went on trial Monday on charges that they accepted bribes as they colluded with gamblers who made hundreds of thousands of dollars betting on individual pitches.
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz went on trial Monday on charges that they accepted bribes as they colluded with gamblers who made hundreds of thousands of dollars betting on individual pitches.

Their careers and possibly their freedom are at stake in the jury trial in Brooklyn federal court. Jury selection got underway after the players arrived in court in the morning. Several professional baseball players, including catchers and baseball executives, are among witnesses expected to testify at a monthlong trial.

Clase, the Guardians' former closer, and Ortiz, a starter, have pleaded not guilty to conspiracy charges and are on non-disciplinary leave from the club without pay while their fate is determined.

According to an indictment, the pitchers accepted several thousand dollars in payoffs to help two gamblers from their native Dominican Republic win at least $460,000 on in-game prop bets on the speed and outcome of certain pitches.

Prosecutors allege that Clase began providing the bettors with information about his pitches in 2023 and recruited Ortiz into the scheme in 2025. Lawyers for Ortiz unsuccessfully sought to have Ortiz tried separately from Clase.

Clase, 28, is a three-time All-Star and two-time American League Reliever of the Year who had completed his fourth season of a $20 million, five-year contract when charges against the pitchers were revealed in November 2025.

Ortiz, 27, had earned $782,600 as a starting pitcher for the Guardians during the 2025 season.

The pitchers have been charged with wire fraud conspiracy, honest services wire fraud conspiracy, money laundering conspiracy and conspiracy to influence sporting contests by bribery.

Defense lawyers are expected to argue that the pitchers did not collude with gamblers and instead were varying the placement of pitches strategically to fool batters.

On Friday, Judge Kiyo A. Matsumoto, who is presiding over the trial, ruled that prosecutors cannot show the jury proof that Clase owed $500,000 in U.S. taxes because they had only provided the evidence to defense lawyers several days earlier and long after a deadline had passed to turn over evidence to their adversaries.

A prosecutor had argued that the government wanted to put the evidence in the trial to offset any claim by Clase's lawyers that he had no incentive to collude with gamblers because he had several million dollars in financial accounts in the Dominican Republic.

Major League Baseball and the Guardians have both said they've fully cooperated with authorities. MLB has said it contacted federal law enforcement when it began investigating unusual betting activity.

articles.title: MLB Insider Projects Teruaki Sato's Contract in 2026 Free Agency Amid Mets Rumors
articles.summary: Japanese star Teruaki Sato "should blow away" the salaries compatriots Kazuma Okamoto and Munetaka Murakami earned last offseason in MLB free agency, according to The Athletic's Keith Law.
articles.body:
Japanese star Teruaki Sato "should blow away" the salaries compatriots Kazuma Okamoto and Munetaka Murakami earned last offseason in MLB free agency, according to The Athletic's Keith Law .

Law projected Sato to earn at least $25 million annually on a deal running for four or five years.

Okamoto got four years and $60 million from the Toronto Blue Jays, while Murakami signed with the Chicago White Sox for two years and $34 million .

Their success in 2026 may give teams more confidence about how Sato will adjust to MLB pitching. Okamoto had 33 home runs and 92 RBI. Murakami looks like a bargain after finishing with 35 homers and a 130 OPS+.

Sato should also benefit from the state of this year's free-agent class.

Two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal is the only true star available, and the position player group is headlined by Randy Arozarena, Seiya Suzuki and Brandon Lowe. Teams with cash to burn may have to pay a premium for a proven hitter.

Sato earned an NPB Triple Crown this season, batting .306 to go along with 39 homers and 106 RBI. Across his six-year career in the league, he owns a .273/.338/.516 slash line.

The New York Mets could make an aggressive play for the 27-year-old. SNY's Chelsea Janes reported traveled personally to Japan on a scouting mission.

Back in August, the New York Post 's Jon Heyman reported the New York Yankees, Los Angeles Dodgers and Philadelphia Phillies could also be in the mix.

A potential work stoppage is hanging over the entire offseason. A lot of free agents may be in a holding pattern until a new collective bargaining agreement is in place.

In the case of Sato and others posted by NPB teams, USA Today 's Bob Nightengale reported they may have to agree to a contract by Dec. 1, the day the current CBA expires.

Sato won't have the luxury of waiting to see how the market evolves all winter before he has to solidify his next move.

articles.title: Posted NPB, KBO players reportedly must sign before current MLB CBA expires on Dec. 1
articles.summary: As of Nov. 1, pitchers Kaima Taira and Hiromi Itoh and infielders Teruaki Sato and Si-Hwan Roh are free to negotiate with all 30 MLB teams.
articles.body:
The 2026 MLB postseason just ended, and now everyone is looking ahead to Dec. 1, 2026.

On that date, the Collective Bargaining Agreement ends, and a lockout between players and ownership is expected to begin. One under-the-radar aspect of a lockout is how it affects this year's crop of international players hoping to sign with an MLB team.

The Athletic's Ken Rosenthal reported that the negotiation window for players posted from Japan's NPB or Korea's KBO won't pause because of the looming lockout, meaning that posted players must sign by 5 p.m. ET on Dec. 1.

On Nov. 1, four players from NPB and KBO were posted. Pitchers Kaima Taira and Hiromi Itoh and infielders Teruaki Sato and Si-Hwan Roh are now free to negotiate with all 30 MLB teams.

Last year's class featured Munetaka Murakami (Chicago White Sox), Kazuma Okamoto (Toronto Blue Jays) and Tatsuya Imai (Houston Astros).

One big difference this year is that the negotiations will have to move quickly. The previous lockout, ahead of the 2021-2022 season, paused the league's international negotiation window. Rosenthal reported that won't happen this year.

Posted international players from the NPB have 45 days to negotiate a deal with an MLB team. If they don't reach an agreement, they return to their Japanese team. That is technically still the case, but players won't actually have 45 days this year. Instead, if they want to agree to a deal, they must complete it by 5 p.m. ET on Dec. 1, before the CBA expires. With their posting becoming official on Nov. 1, that effectively gives them 30 days to close a deal.

Under the current CBA, KBO players have 30 days to sign, and that time frame remains the same. Roh will have the typical 30-day window, which also ends at 5 p.m. ET on Dec. 1.

Sato might be a recognizable player to fans who watched the 2026 World Baseball Classic. He played for Team Japan and went 3-for-10 at the plate. All three hits were doubles.

He was the Central League's best player in Nippon Professional Baseball this year. He won the Triple Crown, leading the league in batting average (.306), home runs (39) and RBI (106). The 27-year-old Sato also won his second consecutive MVP award.

The 26-year-old Taira pitched in 23 games this year and worked to a 12-5 record with a 1.36 ERA. Itoh, 29, made 26 appearances in NPB and posted a 10-10 record with a 3.18 ERA.

Roh is the lone KBO player posted so far. The 25-year-old slashed .283/.360/.505 with 29 home runs and 96 RBI this season.

articles.title: Robinson Cano Jr.'s Marlins Contract Revealed in New Rumors, What to Know About Son of MLB Legend

articles.body:
According to multiple reports, the Miami Marlins signed Robinson Canó Jr. on Monday to a deal worth $1 million.

Canó is the son of longtime MLB star Robinson Canó, who was an eight-time All-Star and one-time World Series champion during his career.

He had stints with the New York Yankees (2005-13), Seattle Mariners (2014-18), New York Mets (2019-20, 2022), San Diego Padres (2022) and Atlanta Braves (2022) during his career, posting a .839 OPS and 335 homers.

The younger Canó, 16, would be a part of Miami's 2028 international class . The Marlins would be thrilled if he ultimately has anything close to resembling his father's MLB career.

Luis Hernández, 17, is currently considered the top international prospect in the sport, per MLB.com . Across 74 games in the Rookie League and Single-A levels with the San Francisco Giants' farm system in 2026 he hit .277 with eight homers, 54 RBI, 51 runs, six stolen bases and a .817 OPS.

articles.title: Si-Hwan Roh Posted for MLB Teams, Top Landing Spots for Korean Star in Free Agency
articles.summary: Si-Hwan Roh is heading to Major League Baseball.
articles.body:
Si-Hwan Roh is heading to Major League Baseball.

The 25-year-old Korean star was posted by the KBO's Hanwha Eagles on Monday, creating a 30-day window for him to negotiate with MLB teams.

But which teams might be interested in his services?

Really, any team needing help at third base—assuming MLB teams believe he's good enough to stick there defensively—or teams willing to utilize him as a designated hitter will likely have interest, especially in a winter that is pretty light on help at the position. Teams that miss out on what is expected to be a vibrant market for Japanese star Teruaki Sato could make sense as Roh suitors.

Michael Clair of MLB.com listed the St. Louis Cardinals, New York Yankees, Seattle Mariners and Los Angeles Angels as potential Roh suitors.

The Cardinals have an extremely obvious need at third base, making them a logical potential destination for a player like Roh. And the Korean star also appears to be on the same timeline as a Cardinals team that showed growth in 2026 but it still very much in a rebuilding process.

The Yankees need to rework their offense in general and will need to replace the likely-departing Jazz Chisholm Jr. and Trent Grisham. They also already are dealing with a large payroll, so a player like Roh might ultimately be a worthwhile gamble at a lower price point than a player like Sato.

The Mariners have a need at third base and a need for more power, though Roh becomes less appealing for Seattle if the team doesn't feel like he can handle the hot corner defensively.

And the Angels... could use some hope. Something to give their fans a reason to get excited as the Stan Kroenke ownership era is set to begin at some point in 2027. Roh wouldn't move the needle like Sato, but it would be a start.

articles.title: MLB Qualifying Contract Offers Tracker and Updates Ahead of 2026 MLB Free Agency
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers may still be celebrating their World Series title, but MLB teams are already looking ahead to the 2027 season and what figures to be a busy offseason.
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers may still be celebrating their World Series title, but MLB teams are already looking ahead to the 2027 season and what figures to be a busy offseason.

One of the first steps of that offseason is the qualifying offer system, which allows teams to make a one-year qualifying offer to impending free agents as long as they have never received such an offer in the past. If a player who receives the offer signs elsewhere, their former team will receive draft-pick compensation.

This year's qualifying offer for the 2027 season is $23.15 million, and players who receive it have until 4 p.m. ET on Nov. 17 to decide whether they accept it. Those who accept it will remain with their team on the one-year deal, while those who reject it will become free agents.

Here is a look at everyone who received the offer.

The Seattle Mariners extended outfielder Randy Arozarena the qualifying offer, per ESPN's Jeff Passan .

The Chicago Cubs extended outfielder Seiya Suzuki the qualifying offer, per ESPN's Jeff Passan .

The Pittsburgh Pirates extended second baseman Brandon Lowe the qualifying offer, per ESPN's Jeff Passan .

The Baltimore Orioles extended pitcher Trevor Rogers the qualifying offer, per ESPN's Jeff Passan .

The San Diego Padres extended pitcher Adrian Morejon the qualifying offer, per ESPN's Jeff Passan .

The New York Yankees extended pitcher David Bednar the qualifying offer, per ESPN's Jeff Passan .

The Milwaukee Brewers extended first baseman Jake Bauers the qualifying offer, per ESPN's Jeff Passan .

The Minnesota Twins extended catcher Ryan Jeffers the qualifying offer, per ESPN's Jeff Passan .

articles.title: Mariners' Randy Arozarena, Cubs' Seiya Suzuki among 8 players receiving $23.15 million qualifying offers
articles.summary: Players have until Nov. 17 to accept or decline the offer.
articles.body:
Eight MLB players received qualifying offers on Monday. The one-year offers are worth $23.15 million.

Players must decide whether to accept the offer by Nov. 17.

Qualifying offers are similar to NFL franchise tags, but with some key differences. QOs can be offered only to impending free agents who have never received a qualifying offer before and who spent the entire regular season with that organization; players who were traded are not eligible.

A player can accept the one-year offer and return to their previous team, or decline it. If they decline it, their former team gets a compensatory pick, and their new team loses a draft pick.

The former team's comp pick can come after the first round, after Competitive Balance Round B, or after the fourth round. The pick's value depends on whether the former team is a competitive balance tax payer (after round four), a revenue sharing recipient (after round one or after Competitive Balance Round B), or neither (after Competitive Balance Round B).

2026 was Arozarena's second full season in Seattle. He had a much better campaign, slashing .281/.381/.484 in 154 games and was named to the American League All-Star team.

The Mariners outfielder hit 26 home runs and drove in 79 runs. Even playing half his games at T-Mobile Park, Arozarena hit 26 home runs, the second-most in his eight-year career.

Re-signing Arozarena is one of the Mariners' biggest offseason to-do items. The other main objective is finding a new manager. Seattle fired Dan Wilson following a 76-86 record.

Suzuki has spent his entire five-year career with the Chicago Cubs. The 31-year-old outfielder played in 143 games last season and hit .270 with 26 home runs and 86 RBI. His 5.1 WAR is easily the highest mark of his Chicago tenure, easily surpassing his previous high of 3.5 in 2024.

Lowe signed with the Pittsburgh Pirates last offseason to bring much-needed power to the Bucs lineup.

The second baseman played in 150 games and launched 35 home runs, easily leading the team. Oneil Cruz had the second-most home runs for the Pirates with 20.

Lowe's had 96 RBI, the second-most of his career, and his .260 batting average was the highest since the 2020 shortened season.

Rogers has been with the Baltimore Orioles since the franchise acquired him from the Miami Marlins in 2024. The southpaw made 30 starts last year. He went 10-11 with a 4.03 ERA.

He led Baltimore in wins and pitched the second-most innings for the team (169 2/3), behind only Shane Baz (179 2/3).

Morejon made 76 appearances for the San Diego Padres last season, a career high. The lefty reliever went 9-3 with a 2.83 ERA. He struck out 107 batters in 86 innings.

Before this year, Morejon punched out 71 batters in 63 2/3 innings in 2024, but breezed past that previous career high in 2026.

2026 was Bednar's first full season with the New York Yankees. He made 64 appearances, tallying a 7-3 record with a 2.47 ERA. Bednar saved 35 games, the second-most in a single season of his career.

The righty blew four saves, tied for the second-most in his career. His seven wins were tied for the most by a New York reliever last season.

Bauers is coming off a World Series win with the Milwaukee Brewers, the first in franchise history.

The first baseman is coming off a career season. He played in 144 games and slashed .266/.389/.484 with 26 home runs and 86 RBI, all career bests.

Bauers led the Brewers in home runs and on-base percentage during the regular season. He struggled with consistency at the plate in the postseason, batting just .191, but he added one home run and six RBI.

Jeffers is likely the top catcher who was set to hit the market this offseason. The 29-year-old played in 92 games this year. He missed time due to a fractured hamate bone in his left wrist that kept him out for nearly two months.

The Minnesota Twins catcher hit .256 this season with 14 home runs and 56 RBI. Jeffers posted a 2.8 WAR, the eighth-highest among catchers last season.

articles.title: Tigers cut ties with four-time All-Star, decline $12 million option
articles.summary: The 39-year-old blew six saves and lost six games in 2026
articles.body:
The Detroit Tigers are looking for a new closer.

Kenley Jansen, who in 2026 moved into third place on baseball's all-time saves leaderboard, is a free agent after the Tigers declined his $12 million contract option for 2027. Detroit will pay Jansen a $2 million buyout instead — one of several roster decisions the team made Monday, Nov. 2.

Jansen recorded a team-leading 22 saves and pitched to a 3.20 ERA in 50 games. He struck out 51 batters in 45 innings, suggesting he still has the stuff to succeed in his 18th major league season after turning 39 in September.

Jansen also blew six saves and lost six games in relief. The team that signs him will be betting on somewhat of a bounceback season from the 6-foot-5 closer whose 498 career saves trail only Mariano Rivera and Trevor Hoffman, both Hall of Famers, on MLB's all-time list.

Jansen has made 983 appearances, the most among active pitchers, in a 17-year career with the Los Angeles Dodgers (2010-21), Atlanta Braves (2022), Boston Red Sox (2023-24), Los Angeles Angels (2025) and Tigers.

In addition to his four All-Star game nods, Jansen has won the Hoffman Award, given to the National League's best relief pitcher twice (2016, 2017). He helped the Dodgers reach the World Series in 2017, 2018 and 2020, winning the latter.

In other Tigers moves, pitcher Drew Anderson's $10 million option for 2027 by the team. The right-hander posted a 3.67 ERA in 49 games in 2026, his first season in MLB after returning from the KBO.

Pitcher Jacob Waguespack signed with the Tigers on a one-year, $1.3 million contract after going 2-2 with a 2.49 ERA in 35 games (one start) for Detroit in 2026. According to Jason Beck of MLB.com, the right-hander can earn an additional $200,000 in innings-based incentives.

articles.title: Phillies’ perfect trade offer for Dodgers’ Teoscar Hernandez
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Phillies do not need another recognizable name simply to make their offseason look ambitious. They need a right-handed hitter who improves t...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Phillies do not need another recognizable name simply to make their offseason look ambitious. They need a right-handed hitter who improves their offensive balance without requiring a franchise-altering investment.

Teoscar Hernandez presents that opportunity.

The Dodgers outfielder has emerged as a trade candidate as Los Angeles considers reshaping its roster. Philadelphia, meanwhile, offers a logical landing spot because of its left-handed-heavy lineup and need for more outfield production.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

A Marsh-and-Ferrebus package would offer Los Angeles immediate major-league help and longer-term upside. For the Phillies, its success would depend on Hernández delivering a meaningful offensive improvement.

Why Teoscar Hernandez fits Philadelphia's offensive needs

Hernandez would bring a different offensive profile to Philadelphia's outfield, but the Phillies must evaluate the current player rather than the reputation.

He batted .267/.334/.425 with 16 home runs in 2026, producing a 110 wRC+, according to MLB Trade Rumors. That metric adjusts for league and ballpark conditions, placing his offensive production approximately 10 percent above average.

Marsh, meanwhile, finished with a .260 average, 18 home runs, 62 RBIs and a .712 OPS. Hernández's .759 OPS represents an improvement, but his lower home run total makes clear this is not automatically a dramatic power upgrade.

The appeal is lineup balance and the possibility of stronger right-handed production. Philadelphia should view Hernandez as another credible run producer, not the centerpiece expected to solve every offensive shortcoming.

His defensive limitations complicate the picture. MLB Trade Rumors describes him as increasingly suited to designated hitter work, an important consideration for any team planning to use him regularly in the outfield.

Moving Marsh would open playing time, but the Phillies would still need a clear defensive plan. Replacing one outfielder with another does not guarantee a better overall unit.

The perfect Phillies trade offer for Hernandez

Philadelphia should explore the following framework:

Marsh would give Los Angeles an established major-league replacement rather than leaving the Dodgers entirely dependent on prospects. His 2026 production demonstrates that he could contribute immediately, even if he would not replicate Hernandez's right-handed offensive profile.

Ferrebus supplies the developmental incentive.

MLB Pipeline ranks him ninth in Philadelphia's system. Across two minor-league levels in 2026, he hit .310/.363/.493 with 11 home runs and 58 RBIs in 328 plate appearances.

That performance makes him a meaningful addition, not a prospect included merely to complete the paperwork. His 12.8 percent strikeout rate also provides an encouraging indicator of contact ability, although minor-league success does not guarantee major-league production.

The combination gives Los Angeles two separate sources of value, an immediate outfield contributor and a young hitter with room to develop.

Why Philadelphia must be disciplined about the price

Philadelphia would surrender a productive major-league outfielder and a top-10 organizational prospect for a veteran whose recent performance suggests a modest upgrade rather than a transformational one.

Hernandez also carries financial obligations. His contract includes a $14.5 million salary for 2027, with $8 million deferred, plus a $15 million club option for 2028 featuring a $6.5 million buyout. Those commitments must be considered alongside the prospect cost.

The deal becomes compelling only if the Phillies trust Hernandez's offensive fit and can accommodate the defensive trade-off. Marsh and Ferrebus offer enough legitimate value to start a serious conversation. Philadelphia should require a clear roster improvement before finishing it.

articles.title: Braves’ Gold Glove Haul Proves Defense Still Wins In Atlanta
articles.summary: Matt Olson and Mauricio Dubón lead a Braves defense that dominates the 2026 Gold Glove awards, proving fielding wins championships.
articles.body:
The 2026 Gold Glove awards landed on Sunday with a clear message for the rest of the league: the Atlanta Braves are built on grit. Matt Olson and Mauricio Dubón did not just make the list; they own it. Olson secured his fourth career award, while Dubón added his third to a resume that already includes wins in 2023 and 2025. This isn't luck. It is a system that values range and hands over raw power.

While the Boston Red Sox and Arizona Diamondbacks tied for the most winners with three each, the Braves made sure their stars stood out in the crowd. According to ESPN , Olson previously won the honor in 2018, 2019, and 2025, showing a consistency that few first basemen can match. The Red Sox got hype for Wilyer Abreu, who took his third straight title, and Ceddanne Rafaela, who won for the second year running. But in Atlanta, we know that one or two elite defenders can change the entire complexion of a playoff series.

Mauricio Dubón earned his third Gold Glove, underscoring his defensive value. He covers ground that most utility men can only dream of. Per Fox Sports , the utility category uses a specific Society for American Baseball Research defensive index to calculate the winners. This means Dubón didn't just look good on tape; the numbers backed him up too.

The 2021 title run was built on players who could move around the diamond without losing a step. Dubón fits that mold perfectly. He plays multiple spots, makes the tough plays, and keeps the defense stable when the lineup gets shaky. It is a quiet skill, but it wins games.

Winning these awards is harder now than it was a decade ago. Since 2013, the voting has mixed the eyes of managers and coaches with hard data from the SABR defensive index. That data makes up about 25% of the total vote, according to reports from Fox Sports. This shift stops voters from just picking the guy with the best highlight reel.

While managers and a maximum of six coaches per team submit the votes, they are prohibited from selecting players from their own club. This rule forces them to look at the league as a whole. It prevents bias and forces a true comparison of skill. When a player like Olson or Dubón wins under these rules, it means they are truly the best in the game. No flukes. No home-field advantage in the voting booth.

The money attached to these wins is small, but the prestige is huge. Walker earned a $75,000 bonus for his win, while Turang took home $25,000. The Braves have now secured multiple awards in a season where the competition was fierce. That is the standard we set. The 2026 Gold Gloves were awarded in Atlanta.
